paragraphs.text: That is, vain words, and without consolation?
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Meaning, with matters that are of no importance, which are forgotten as soon as they are uttered, as the East wind dries up moisture as soon as it falls.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He charges Job as though his talk caused men to cast off the fear of God and prayer.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: You speak as the mockers and contemners of God do.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: That is, the most ancient and so by reason the most wise?
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Are you only wise?
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: He accuses Job's pride and ingratitude, that will not be comforted by God, but by their counsel.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Why do you stand in your own conceit?
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: His purpose is to prove that Job, as an unjust man and a hypocrite, is punished for his sins, as he did before, Job 4:8.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: Who has a desire to sin, as he who is thirsty to drink.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: Who by their wisdom so governed, that no stranger invaded them, and so the land seemed to be given to them alone.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: The cruel man is always in danger of death, and is never quiet in conscience.
paragraphs.label: m
paragraphs.anchor: of years is hidden to the

paragraphs.text: Out of that misery to which he once fell.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: God not only impoverishes the wicked often, but even in their prosperity he punishes them with a greediness to gain even more: which is as a beggary.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: He shows the weapons God uses against the wicked, who lift up themselves against him, that is, terror of conscience and outward afflictions.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: That is, he was so puffed up with prosperity and abundance for all things, that he forgave God: noting that Job in his happiness did not have the true fear of God.
paragraphs.label: q

paragraphs.text: Though he build and repair ruinous places to gain fame, yet God will bring all to nothing, and turn his great prosperity into extreme misery.
paragraphs.label: r

paragraphs.text: Meaning, that his sumptuous buildings would never come to perfection.
paragraphs.label: s

paragraphs.text: He stands in his own conceit, that he will give no place to good counsel, therefore his own pride will bring him to destruction.
paragraphs.label: t

paragraphs.text: As one who gathers grapes before they are ripe.
paragraphs.label: u

paragraphs.text: Who were built or maintained by bribery.
paragraphs.label: x

paragraphs.text: Therefore all their vain devises will turn to their own destruction.
paragraphs.label: y
